title: split-test-matrix-and-add-toolchain-compat-adapter
author: Aisha Kapoor
ci_status: pass (two reruns for flaky integration lane)
description:
Motivation: Presubmit CI has grown noisy and slow as we expanded integration coverage. Two pain points: (1) the monolithic test matrix runs heavy integration suites on most PRs, increasing feedback time; (2) inconsistent toolchain probing across runners causes subtle failures (node/go mismatches and flaky builds). This PR splits the matrix into fast/critical lanes and heavy integration lanes, and introduces a lightweight Toolchain Compatibility Adapter that standardizes probe, shim, and fallback logic across runners.

What this PR does (summary):
- Split CI into three lanes: fast-smoke (lint, unit, small integration), compatibility-check (toolchain probe + dep health), and heavy-integration (long-running end-to-end tests). The default presubmit now runs fast-smoke + compatibility-check; heavy-integration is gated to staged runs and depends on a quick presubmit pass.
- Add a toolchain adapter written as a minimal Go action (ci/toolchain-adapter) that: probes node, go, and python runtimes from a cached manifest; emits standardized env variables; and provides a deterministic fallback behavior for older runners.
- Add dep-health-check step to the compatibility-check lane: verifies package manager lockfile consistency, flags common transitive issues, and suggests safe pin candidates.
- Adjust caching strategy: split cache keys by lane and by workspace-target to avoid cache poisoning between heavy and fast lanes.
- Bump a small set of build/test deps that surfaced in probe: js-yaml@5.0.1, go-test-runner@v2.1.0, and hermetic-setup@v0.9.2.
- Update release automation hooks so that releases only trigger the heavy-integration gate after a green canary smoke (reduces release risk while shortening initial feedback).

Important notes about rollout and compatibility:
- This change is opt-in for a 48-hour window via the feature flag ci.split_matrix_enabled=false in the repo settings; rollout will be flipped to true after monitoring.
- The toolchain adapter is implemented to be backward compatible with existing runner contracts (it only sets env vars and exits non-zero on fatal mismatches). Older local dev flows remain unchanged when the adapter is not present.

Checklist:
- [x] Split workflows and add gating conditions
- [x] Implement toolchain adapter and unit tests for probe logic
- [x] Add dep-health-check heuristics and docs
- [x] Smoke-tested fast-smoke lane across macOS/Linux/self-hosted runners
- [x] Coordinated release hook change with release-engineering

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Flaky heavy-integration still causes noise when occasionally run on PRs. Mitigation: gated heavy runs and better cache separation; full heavy-suite runs scheduled nightly.
- Risk: Partial rollout might leave some CI runners using old cached manifests. Mitigation: adapter emits warnings and fails explicitly when mismatch is fatal, plus a migration job to refresh caches was included.

How to validate locally:
- Run go test ./ci/toolchain-adapter to validate probe behavior.
- Use scripts/ci/local-smoke.sh to simulate fast-smoke and compatibility-check lanes.

References: ENG-1198 for test-flake triage, ENG-1243 for release gating. Linear and support ticket SUP-453 tracked an incident where runner toolchain drift caused prod test failures.

release_notes: Split CI presubmit to speed feedback: default presubmit runs fast-smoke + compatibility check. Introduced a toolchain compatibility adapter to stabilize runner probes and a dep-health-check step to catch lockfile mismatches earlier. Bumped minor build deps. (ENG-1198, ENG-1243)
notes_for_release_engineering: Switch release pipeline to depend on after-smoke gate only; heavy-integration remains scheduled post-canary. Ensure infra/ci-bastion refresh-cache-job runs during rollout window.
testing_performed: Ran fast-smoke across linux/mac/self-hosted pools; compatibility-check validated against a cached manifest and against an intentionally mismatched manifest; heavy-integration executed in a staged run on a canary branch.
